title: Formulating and Characterizing Lipid Nanoparticles for Gene Delivery using a Microfluidic Mixing Platform
protocol: Prepare 1x PBS using 8 mM Na₂HPO₄, 2 mM KH₂PO₄, 137 mM NaCl, and 2.7 mM KCl in nuclease-free water.
Adjust the pH of PBS to 7.4.
Sterilize PBS by vacuum filtration using a 0.22 µm pore-size filter.
Prepare citrate buffer using 5 mM sodium citrate, 5 mM citric acid, and 150 mM sodium chloride in nuclease-free water.
Adjust the pH of citrate buffer to 4.5.
Sterilize citrate buffer by vacuum filtration using a 0.22 µm pore-size filter.
Prepare malic acid buffer using 20 mM malic acid and 30 mM sodium chloride in nuclease-free water.
Adjust the pH of malic acid buffer to 3.0.
Sterilize malic acid buffer by vacuum filtration using a 0.22 µm pore-size filter.
Solubilize stock lipids in pure 200 proof ethanol if they are in powder form.
Calculate the required volume for each lipid component based on a desired molar ratio of 50:10:39:1 (ionizable lipid:helper lipid:cholesterol:PEG) and a total lipid concentration of 10 mM.
Add the appropriate amount of ionizable lipid stock solution to a glass vial.
Add the helper lipid stock solution to the glass vial.
Add the cholesterol stock solution to the glass vial.
Add the PEG lipid stock solution to the glass vial.
Mix all lipid components with intermittent vortexing.
Calculate and add 200 proof ethanol for a total mixture volume of 533 µL.
Prepare a nucleic acid solution.
Calculate the number of N units using the given formula.
Calculate the P units for the desired N/P ratio.
Calculate the necessary nucleic acid concentration to obtain the required P units using the provided equation.
Determine the mass concentration of mRNA or DNA required based on the calculated moles.
Make up 1.5 mL of 14.88 µg/mL mRNA in citrate buffer.
Draw at least 0.5 mL of ethanol into a 1 mL syringe, ensuring there are no bubbles or air gaps at the syringe tip.
Load this syringe into the right inlet of the cartridge.
Fill a 3 mL syringe with 1.5 mL of aqueous buffer (citrate for RNA and malic acid for DNA), ensuring there are no air bubbles or gaps.
Load this syringe into the left inlet of the cartridge.
Insert two 15 mL conical tubes in the clip holders to serve as waste containers.
Click on Run in the instrument software to begin the mixing.
Open the lid when the bottom blue light shuts off, indicating the instrument has stopped priming.
Properly dispose of the conical tubes and syringes after use.
Update the software with the formulation parameters by clicking on the appropriate fields (Table 2).
Fill a 1 mL syringe with the lipid mix prepared in step 2.
Remove any air gaps or bubbles at the syringe tip.
Insert the syringe into the right side of the cartridge.
Draw the nucleic acid solution prepared in step 3 into a 3 mL syringe.
Ensure there are no bubbles or air gaps in the syringe tip.
Insert the syringe into the left inlet of the cartridge.
Label a 15 mL RNase-free conical tube with the sample name and insert it into the left tube clip.
Place a 15 mL waste conical in the right tube clip.
Close the instrument lid and click Run after confirming correct input of parameters.
Discard the waste container and cartridge after the instrument finishes running.
Retain the conical tube with the LNP sample.
Dilute the LNP 5x with PBS to minimize ethanol concentration to less than 5% (v/v).
Pre-wash an ultra-centrifuge filter (100 kDa pore size) with 2 mL of PBS by centrifuging at 1000 x g for 5 min.
Empty the PBS from the bottom compartment of the ultra-centrifuge filter.
Add diluted LNPs to the top compartment of the pre-washed ultra-centrifuge filter and centrifuge at 1000 x g for 12 min.
Discard the flow-through from the bottom compartment.
Perform two more washes by adding 5 mL of PBS to the ultra-centrifuge filter each time.
Centrifuge at the same parameters for each wash.
Prepare a standard curve by making 2-fold serial dilutions of working nucleic acid solution in PBS, starting with a highest concentration of 500 ng/mL, and making at least five dilutions.
Use PBS as a blank for the standard curve.
Dilute LNP samples with PBS to achieve an approximate theoretical concentration that lies around the mid-point of the standard curve.
Prepare a solution containing 0.5% (v/v) RNA quantification reagent, 0.4% (v/v) TritonX-100, and 99.1% (v/v) PBS.
Prepare a solution of the reagent without TritonX-100, containing 0.5% (v/v) RNA reagent and 99.5% (v/v) PBS.
Load at least four replicates of each LNP and nucleic acid standard solution in a 96-well black fluorescence plate.
Add an equal volume of the reagent with TritonX-100 to half of the replicate wells for total nucleic acid quantification.
Add an equal volume of the reagent without TritonX-100 to the remaining wells for non-encapsulated nucleic acid quantification.
Shake the plate for 5 minutes at room temperature to ensure thorough mixing, avoiding light exposure.
Measure fluorescence using a microplate reader with an excitation wavelength of 480 nm and emission wavelength of 520 nm.
Calculate the concentration of nucleic acid outside of the LNP using the standard curve made without TritonX-100.
Multiply by the dilution factor used in step 7.2.
Calculate the concentration of nucleic acid both inside and outside of the LNP using the standard curve made with TritonX-100.
Multiply by the dilution factor used in step 7.2.
Calculate the concentration of nucleic acid inside by subtracting the concentration of nucleic acid outside from the total concentration of nucleic acid.
Quantify the encapsulation efficiency from the ratio of nucleic acid inside to the total concentration of nucleic acid.
Adjust the nucleic acid concentration within the LNP solution if needed using results from encapsulation efficiency.
If a less concentrated solution is desired, dilute with PBS to achieve the desired concentration.
If a more concentrated solution is desired, perform additional centrifugation runs with an ultra-centrifuge filter.
Dilute an aliquot of the LNP solution 40x with PBS to obtain a final volume of 1 mL.
Dilute an aliquot of the LNP solution 40x with nuclease-free water to obtain a final volume of 1 mL.
Add the diluted LNP solution into a folded capillary zeta cell up to the fill line.
Insert the zeta cell into the instrument, ensuring that the electrodes are making contact with the instrument.

Set up an operating procedure in the instrument software for measuring the zeta potential including measurement type, sample details (material, dispersant, temperature, and cell type), and number of runs.
Begin the measurement acquisition by clicking Start.
